2. Should the page name a preview on Admit? LOCK the draft: never in 0253.
Keep the existing rule: preview binding is checked when the admission names a preview by ID. Do not change `play.js` to automatically name the preview merely because a card displays one.
A preview being visible is not, by itself, proof that the designer intends to rely on that preview as admission evidence. Automatically binding it could create new refusals without establishing that the preview was part of the admission decision.
The named-preview path must still have direct row coverage. STUDIO-owned tests can exercise it without changing the normal page workflow.
his rulings.3:
3. Should FLAGSHIP-0 name the preview it verified? LOCK the draft: never.
Keep FLAGSHIP-0's rule that studio admission does not read its evidence. Do not amend the row to name the preview.
This preserves the distinction between an external procedure's evidence and the authority decision made by the studio. If a future workflow deliberately makes admission depend on a preview, that should be a separately specified contract—not an implicit change to FLAGSHIP-0.
